name: Projekt Reward Vault unbacked purchase-delta allocations
summary: The FTP ETH-reflection vault's trackPurchase, called from registered tokens' transfer hooks, credited a holder's token-balance increase as a purchase without checking it was a genuine buy. Attackers flash-donated WETH to a token pair and skimmed tokens to fresh holders (later copycats cycled tokens between wallets), then withdrew the unbacked ETH.

campaign.selection: transactions with an internal ETH transfer out of vault 0x574fc478bc45ce144105fa44d98b4b2e4bd442cb after the 0x90f40d3c drain (Etherscan txlistinternal): copycat skim and wallet-chain trackPurchase withdrawals

notes: The earliest exploit is 0x325c97b5's Balancer-flash WETH donation and skim on the DIAMND pair (0xd0a5b433), followed in the same block by its 31.36 ETH withdraw; the July drain repeated it over 13 tokens. Reset is DIAMND's registration in the vault, the listing this anchor needed.

Loss is every ETH outflow of the vault over the anchor, the July drain and the copycat bundle (the vault fell from 432 ETH to dust), each bundle day priced at its DefiLlama ETH quote. A few ordinary holder claims inside the bundle window are not separated; they are negligible.
